the brain architecture of race CP in adults is the result of the acquisition of racial labels during childhood.
language acquisition modulated the neural architecture of CP, with a more modularized network in adults than children, and with a unique activation of the STG and IFG in adults.

the acquisition of linguistic labels during childhood, which are used to categorize social groups (such as race), modulates the neural organization of race categorical perception.
the acquisition of language during childhood modulates brain network connectedness when perceiving racial categories.
the neural correlates of race CP are already in place in children, but they are modulated by the acquisition of language.
